papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and machine learning to identify a prognostic gene signature related to tumor doubling time in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, potentially guiding treatment decisions. The authors also explore therapeutic targets linked to this signature, offering a new avenue for personalized therapy in HNSCC.

papers.title: A multi-omics integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition prognostic signature in tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes, highlighting the critical need for dependable prognostic indicators. The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a fundamental biological process driving cancer progression. This study aimed to develop and independently validate an EMT-associated gene expression signature for predicting prognosis in TSCC through a multi-omics strategy.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) prognostic signature for tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) by integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. The signature independently predicts patient outcomes, offering a potentially reliable clinical tool for risk stratification in this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Deciphering lung cancer at high resolution: a narrative review of applications of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics sequencing.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Many patients are still facing limited treatment benefit or therapeutic resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution characterization of cellular states, whereas spatial transcriptomics (ST) preserves tissue architecture and maps gene expression within the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review summarizes recent advances in scRNA-seq and ST in lung cancer and discusses how these technologies have improved our understanding of tumor biology and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics applied to lung cancer, highlighting how these high-resolution technologies have improved understanding of tumor biology and therapeutic response. It discusses the contributions of these methods in characterizing cellular states and mapping gene expression within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: SPAE: Deciphering Cell Cycle Dynamics and Cell States in Single-cell RNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology have enabled the investigation of gene expression changes at the single-cell level, particularly for elucidating the heterogeneity among cells and complex biological processes. This technique reveals subtle molecular differences within individual cells, thereby offering a unique viewpoint for the investigation of cell cycle progression, cellular differentiation, and disease pathogenesis. However, accurately identifying and analyzing cell cycle dynamics in scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of the data and
papers.summary: This paper introduces SPAE, a new computational method for deciphering cell cycle dynamics and cell states from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying cell cycle phases in complex scRNA-seq datasets, providing a tool that could improve understanding of cellular heterogeneity and differentiation.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects panels of marker genes for cell types by framing the problem as a minimal set-covering optimization, rather than relying on one-gene-at-a-time differential expression. Applied to neocortical neural stem cell data, it identifies gene panels that better capture developmental progression and cell identity. This approach improves the specificity and interpretability of cell type markers in single-cell RNA-seq atlases.

papers.title: Landscape of Cell States and Multicellular Ecotypes in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most prevalent type of lung cancer and remains a major global health burden. Comprehensive characterization of tumor microenvironment (TME) heterogeneity is critical for understanding tumor progression and clinical outcomes in NSCLC. In this study, we identified 34 transcriptionally defined cell states and 6 multicellular ecotypes using the EcoTyper framework, thereby systematically delineating the TME landscape of NSCLC. These cell states and ecotypes were further validated across 11 independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts, one single-cell RNA sequenc
papers.summary: This study uses the EcoTyper framework to identify 34 transcriptionally defined cell states and 6 multicellular ecotypes in non-small cell lung cancer, systematically characterizing the tumor microenvironment. The findings are validated across multiple independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset, providing a comprehensive landscape of NSCLC TME heterogeneity.

papers.title: An Integrated Transcriptional and Post-Transcriptional Regulatory Circuit Orchestrated by NUDT21 Maintains the Proliferation and Survival of Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor, associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21 as a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation (APA) in neuroblastoma, revealing an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that maintains tumor cell proliferation and survival. The findings highlight APA as a novel therapeutic target in this pediatric cancer.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a versatile transcriptomic aging clock that accurately predicts biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework, Pasta maps chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation, offering a broadly applicable tool for aging research.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging role of spatial biology techniques, particularly spatial transcriptomics, in understanding cancer epigenetics within the tissue microenvironment. It highlights how these methods preserve tissue architecture and can reveal spatially restricted epigenetic regulatory programs that influence tumor heterogeneity and cell communication.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study presents a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye, overcoming the technical challenge of melanin interference by using a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method compatible with immunohistochemistry. The authors generated a comprehensive atlas of pigmented tissue development and complemented it with re-analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data, providing a valuable resource for understanding eye development and related disorders.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This paper introduces a contextual activity score (CAS) to infer ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data, overcoming limitations of the standard Alu Editing Index (AEI) which requires raw sequencing reads and is unsuitable for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. CAS enables ADAR activity estimation across diverse transcriptomic technologies, potentially facilitating studies in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), revealing shared tumor-specific transcripts that could serve as a common reservoir for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that neoTSTs may overcome the limitation of low mutation-derived antigen availability, offering a promising target for vaccine development in HCC.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a CDH3-Associated Malignant Epithelial State and Immunosuppressive Niche to Predict Prognosis in Thymic Epithelial Tumors.
papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies whose aggressive epithelial states and microenvironmental organization remain poorly defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, bulk transcriptomics, functional assays, xenograft validation, and computational pathology to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in TETs. We identified a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state located at the origin of malignant-state trajectories and enriched for stem-like and EMT-related features. Spatial transc
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in thymic epithelial tumors, identifying a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state with stem-like and EMT features that predicts prognosis and is linked to an immunosuppressive niche. The findings provide new insights into TET biology and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication (CCC), organizing them into three groups based on their analytical frameworks. It highlights how spatial context improves CCC inference over single-cell RNA-seq alone, and provides a structured guide to help researchers select appropriate methods for their biological questions.

papers.title: Tissue-level division of labor is coordinated across organs through universal programs and context-specific adaptations.
papers.abstract: Fibroblasts, macrophages, and endothelial cells are common to most mammalian tissues, where they support homeostasis, repair, and immune regulation. Yet, how they coordinate functions across tissue environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze single-cell RNA sequencing data from 16 human tissues by using Pareto optimality and identify 15 archetypes- specialized programs reflecting functional tradeoffs. These include universal archetypes shared across tissues and tissue-specific archetypes shaped by local context. We show that tissues span a continuous archetype-distribution axis from metabol
papers.summary: This study analyzes single-cell RNA sequencing data from 16 human tissues to uncover how shared cell types (fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelial cells) coordinate their functions across different tissue environments. Using Pareto optimality, the authors identify 15 archetypes—specialized gene expression programs reflecting functional tradeoffs—that include both universal programs shared across tissues and tissue-specific adaptations. The findings reveal a continuous axis of archetype distribution across tissues, providing insight into how tissue-level division of labor is coordinated.

papers.title: The Hsd17b13P260S patient variant knock-in male mouse model provides translational insights into HSD17B13 biology.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent liver disease that can progress to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a condition marked by inflammation and fibrosis that increases the risk of cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Loss-of-function (LoF) variants of hydroxysteroid 17-β dehydrogenase 13 (HSD17B13), a lipid droplet-associated enzyme, protect against progression from MASLD to MASH and more severe types of liver disease.
papers.summary: This study characterizes a new mouse model carrying the human HSD17B13 P260S patient variant, which is associated with protection against liver disease progression. The findings provide translational insights into HSD17B13 biology and its role in MASLD/MASH, supporting the development of therapies targeting this enzyme.

papers.title: Myasthenia thymus reprograms class-switched B cells into BAFF-dependent survivors.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) presents a clinical challenge where autoantibody titers poorly predict disease severity, and thymectomy provides inconsistent benefits. We hypothesized that thymic B cells acquire survival mechanisms that bypass canonical tolerance checkpoints, enabling persistence independent of antigen-specific selection. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, V(D)J repertoire analysis, and spatial transcriptomics to generate the largest MG atlas to date (237,661 cells), we identified a tolerance checkpoint swap in MG pathogenesis. Pathological class-switched B cells within thymic germinal
papers.summary: This study generated a large single-cell and spatial transcriptomics atlas of the myasthenia gravis (MG) thymus, revealing that pathological class-switched B cells in thymic germinal centers are reprogrammed to become BAFF-dependent survivors, bypassing normal tolerance checkpoints. This provides new insights into why autoantibody titers poorly correlate with disease severity and why thymectomy has inconsistent benefits, suggesting BAFF as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Cross-trait genetic analysis maps shared polygenic architecture between primary aldosteronism and blood pressure to adrenal cell states.
papers.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a major cause of endocrine hypertension and contributes substantially to blood pressure (BP)-related morbidity. Although aldosterone excess directly raises BP, the extent to which genetic susceptibility to PA overlaps with the broader polygenic architecture of BP remains unclear. We aimed to characterise the shared genetic architecture between PA and BP traits and to place shared genetic signals within adrenal tissue context.
papers.summary: This study uses cross-trait genetic analysis to map the shared polygenic architecture between primary aldosteronism (PA) and blood pressure (BP), revealing significant genetic overlap. The shared signals are localized to specific adrenal cell states, providing new insights into the genetic basis of PA and its relationship to BP regulation.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Architecture of the Liver Structural Organization, Methodological Advances, and Functional Implications.
papers.abstract: Though comprising only 2-3% of body weight, the liver performs more than 500 distinct biochemical tasks, despite a parenchyma built almost entirely of hepatocytes-a single cell type that alone metabolizes carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, synthesizes plasma proteins, produces bile, and detoxifies xenobiotics. How one cell type achieves this breadth turns out to depend on three-dimensional architecture and the zonal gradients it creates. Anatomists have offered many frameworks for this organization: the classical hexagonal lobule, the portal lobule, the metabolic acinus, and the modular poly
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes historical and modern frameworks for understanding liver three-dimensional architecture, emphasizing how zonal gradients and structural organization enable a single cell type—hepatocytes—to perform over 500 metabolic tasks. It highlights methodological advances in imaging and spatial analysis that are refining our view of liver function and disease.

papers.title: Tumor NLRP3 Amplification Promotes Immunotherapy Resistance by Inhibiting STAT1 Signaling and MHC Class I Expression.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy resistance remains a challenge in immuno-oncology and predictive biomarkers are needed to guide combination immunotherapy selection for the individual patient. We show that elevated tumor-intrinsic NOD-, LRR-, and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) signaling activity correlates with checkpoint inhibitor resistance in several independent cohorts of stage III/IV melanoma and gastroesophageal (GE) adenocarcinoma patients. In situ hybridization demonstrates that tumor NLRP3 copy-number gain is observed in immunotherapy resistant melanomas and GE adenocarcinomas harboring enhan
papers.summary: This study identifies tumor-intrinsic NLRP3 signaling as a driver of immunotherapy resistance in melanoma and gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, showing that NLRP3 copy-number gain inhibits STAT1 signaling and MHC class I expression. Elevated NLRP3 activity correlates with checkpoint inhibitor resistance across multiple patient cohorts, suggesting it could serve as a predictive biomarker for guiding combination immunotherapy selection.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies SMIM24 as a favorable prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) exhibits substantial molecular and clinical heterogeneity, contributing to variable disease progression and therapeutic outcomes. We previously identified a de-clear cell differentiation (DCCD) tumor state characterized by loss of canonical clear-cell features and aggressive clinical behavior. This study aimed to translate DCCD-associated biology into a prognostic framework and investigate its underlying molecular basis. Using TCGA-KIRC as the training cohort, we developed a five-gene prognostic signature comprising COL7A1, IGFN1, AJAP1, SMIM24, and ADGR
papers.summary: This study develops a five-gene prognostic signature for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) based on a de-clear cell differentiation (DCCD) tumor state, and identifies SMIM24 as a favorable prognostic biomarker through integrative multi-omics analysis. The findings provide a potential framework for risk stratification and highlight SMIM24's role in ccRCC prognosis.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the naive-to-primed pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The authors uncover an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3, which orchestrates the transcriptional and epigenetic changes required for this transition.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics in Plants: From Cellular Maps to Mechanistic Insight.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has transformed plant biology by restoring the spatial context lost in bulk and dissociation-based transcriptomic approaches. This review synthesizes recent progress across diverse plant species and tissues, showing that gene expression is not only cell-type specific but also tightly organized by position within organs and developmental niches. Studies of meristems, vascular tissues, and floral organs reveal spatially segregated developmental programs underlying growth and differentiation; seed and grain analyses uncover compartmentalized programs controlling nutrient t
papers.summary: This review highlights how spatial transcriptomics is transforming plant biology by revealing that gene expression is organized by position within organs and developmental niches, not just by cell type. It synthesizes recent findings across meristems, vascular tissues, floral organs, and seeds, showing how spatially segregated programs control growth, differentiation, and nutrient allocation.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal atlas of giant-cell formation during Meloidogyne incognita infection in tomato roots.
papers.abstract: Root-knot nematodes (RKNs; Meloidogyne spp.) are destructive agricultural parasites, but although giant cell formation is required for establishing parasitism, the mechanism of action has not been fully elucidated. Spatial transcriptomics enables precise spatiotemporal analyses of gene expression, facilitating studies of cell heterogeneity. We performed spatial transcriptomic sequencing on Moneymaker tomato root galls caused by M. incognita infection at 3, 5, and 7 days post-inoculation to investigate RKN-induced giant cell formation. Five major cell types were identified; of these, giant cell
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to create a spatiotemporal atlas of giant-cell formation in tomato roots infected by root-knot nematodes, identifying five major cell types and revealing gene expression changes over time. The findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying nematode-induced giant cell development, which is critical for parasitism.

papers.title: Decoding macrophage-driven tumor heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma using spatial and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Macrophages play critical roles in tumorigenesis and progression; however, their functions in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we leveraged multiple perspectives, including bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics, to conduct an integrated analysis of various databases. We identified two macrophage-associated gene signatures, SLC11A1 and IFI30, and established a classifier based on these genes that correlates with different RCC prognoses and molecular patterns. This classifier significantly predicts
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). The authors identify two macrophage-associated gene signatures, SLC11A1 and IFI30, and build a classifier that predicts RCC prognosis and molecular patterns, highlighting the role of macrophages in tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Integrated inference of cellular compositions and gene expression programs by deconvolution.
papers.abstract: While computational deconvolution is routinely used to estimate cell-type proportions from tissue mixtures, reconstructing cell-type-specific transcriptomes at single-sample resolution remains a fundamentally underdetermined algorithmic challenge. Consequently, accurate single-sample, gene-level inference is rarely achieved by existing tools. Here, we systematically benchmarked multiple deconvolution approaches across diverse biological contexts using both pseudo-bulk mixtures and real bulk RNA-seq datasets derived from multiple tissues. Evaluating the critical computational limitations in the
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational deconvolution methods for estimating cell-type proportions and reconstructing cell-type-specific transcriptomes from bulk RNA-seq data, highlighting the underdetermined nature of single-sample gene-level inference. The authors systematically evaluate multiple approaches across diverse tissues and identify key computational limitations, providing guidance for improving accuracy in practical applications.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, identifying potential mediating roles of inflammatory proteins. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa and inflammatory pathways may influence CNS tumor risk, offering new insights into the gut-immune-brain axis.

papers.title: An Explanatory Deep Learning Pipeline for the Prediction and Visualization of Spatially Resolved Biomarker Expression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Histopathologic evaluation remains central to cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, yet the molecular programs underlying distinct tissue morphologies aren't routinely accessible in clinical workflows. Spatial transcriptomic/proteomic platforms provide region-specific molecular measurements but are limited by cost, throughput, and scalability. Most computational pathology models rely on either bulk tissue-based gene expression or a focused gene/protein expression-panel prediction, thereby obscuring subregion-specific morpho-molecular relationships and limiting spatial interpretation of a wi
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning pipeline that predicts spatially resolved biomarker expression directly from histopathology images in triple-negative breast cancer, enabling visualization of molecular patterns without costly spatial profiling. The approach addresses the gap between routine histology and molecular data by providing subregion-specific predictions, which could improve clinical accessibility to molecular information.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence with tissue-specific gene expression in Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF motifs relate to transcriptional activity and chromatin state, filling a gap in integrative genomic visualization tools.

papers.title: Sample Preparation for Imaging-Based Spatial Transcriptomics in Rigid Plant Tissues (Roots, Shoots).
papers.abstract: Plant roots dynamically respond to environmental changes and serve as an ideal system for studying cell development and gene regulation. Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution mapping of gene expression while preserving spatial context. However, existing sample preparation techniques remain inadequate for handling rigid plant tissues such as crop roots. Here, we present a detailed and practical protocol for preparing rigid plant tissue samples for imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. The workflow ensures effective tissue handling while maintaini
papers.summary: This protocol provides a detailed workflow for preparing rigid plant tissues, such as crop roots, for imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, addressing a key technical gap in sample preparation. It enables high-resolution gene expression mapping while preserving spatial context, which is crucial for studying plant development and environmental responses.

papers.title: Myofibroblastic CAF and Malignant Ductal Cell Crosstalk Drives Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition and Progression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma via THBS2-SDC/Integrin Axes.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy with a five-year survival rate below 10%. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastasis, yet the specific CAF subtypes and molecular axes driving PDAC progression remain incompletely understood. Here, using multi-omics data from PDAC samples, we identified a malignant ductal subpopulation, termed Ductal-T0, characterized by the highest EMT activity and prominent acquisition of myofibroblastic CAF (myCAF)-like transcriptional programs. Computationally, we predicted that my
papers.summary: This study identifies a specific malignant ductal cell subpopulation (Ductal-T0) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that exhibits high epithelial-mesenchymal transition activity and myofibroblastic CAF-like features, and predicts that crosstalk between myCAFs and these malignant cells via THBS2-SDC/integrin axes drives tumor progression. The findings provide new insights into CAF-tumor cell interactions and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Identification of Vasculogenic Mimicry-Associated Molecular Subtypes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma for Prognostic Stratification and Therapeutic Response Prediction.
papers.abstract: Objective: Vasculogenic mimicry (VM), characterized by the de novo formation of microvascular-like channels derived from aggressive tumor cells without involving traditional endothelial cells, is a pivotal pathological hallmark driving extreme invasiveness and dismal prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to establish a VM-based molecular subtyping system and systematically characterize its associated biological features, thereby providing a potential framework for individualized prognostic assessment and treatment decision-making in HCC. Methods: We integrated curated V
papers.summary: This study identifies vasculogenic mimicry (VM)-associated molecular subtypes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) using multi-omics data, linking them to distinct prognostic outcomes and therapeutic responses. The proposed subtyping system offers a potential framework for personalized prognosis and treatment decisions in HCC.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method for annotating cell types in single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs) into a heterogeneous graph learning framework. It iteratively refines cell type predictions using regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, improving annotation accuracy over existing methods that ignore this information.

papers.title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) dynamically orchestrate cell fate emergence remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present GRNvelo, a computational framework that reconstructs multiscale cell fate dynamics by integrating GRNs with phenotypic dynamics from temporal single-cell RNA-seq data. GRNvelo establishes a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous multiscale model that couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with nonlocal cell growth-mediated population dynamics. To operationalize this model, GRNvelo devises a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm
papers.summary: GRNvelo is a new computational framework that integrates gene regulatory networks with temporal single-cell RNA-seq data to reconstruct multiscale cell fate dynamics. It couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with population-level growth dynamics using a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm, providing a biologically interpretable model of how gene networks orchestrate cell fate emergence.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper reports a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a new in vitro model for studying ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. The protocol's effectiveness was validated using single-cell RNA-sequencing, which confirmed the expression of markers for transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathways.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals the Potential of ZDHHC16 in Tumor Progression and Immune Regulation.
papers.abstract: S-palmitoylation is a crucial post-translational modification that regulates diverse cellular processes, particularly signalling pathways. The ZDHHC family of enzymes catalyzes this modification, however, the role of ZDHHC16 in cancer warrants in-depth investigation. This study presents a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of ZDHHC16, examining its expression patterns, clinical relevance, associations with immune responses, genomic characteristics, and potential as a therapeutic target. We further analysed single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to identify specific cell populations associa
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of the palmitoyltransferase ZDHHC16, revealing its expression patterns, clinical correlations, immune associations, and genomic features across multiple cancer types. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify specific cell populations linked to ZDHHC16, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target and biomarker in tumor progression and immune regulation.

papers.title: AddaGCN: Spatial transcriptomics deconvolution using graph convolutional networks with adversarial discriminative domain adaptation.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics has substantially improved our understanding of the spatial architecture and gene expression heterogeneity within tissues. However, many spatial transcriptomics techniques can not reach single-cell resolution, instead measuring gene expression profiles from mixtures of potentially heterogeneous cell types. Here we propose AddaGCN, a robust deconvolution method to infer cell type composition from spatial transcriptomic data. AddaGCN leverages graph convolutional networks to incorporate spatial information and adopts an adversarial discriminative
papers.summary: AddaGCN is a new computational method that uses graph convolutional networks and adversarial domain adaptation to infer cell type composition from spatial transcriptomics data, improving deconvolution accuracy by incorporating spatial information. The approach addresses the challenge of mixed cell types in spatial transcriptomics measurements.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm and astrocyte-associated diagnostic and therapeutic model for cirrhosis encephalopathy patients via integrative bioinformatic pipelines and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Cirrhosis encephalopathy (CE) is a severe neuropsychiatric complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by cognitive decline. While circadian rhythm (CR) disruption and astrocyte dysfunction are independently implicated, their integrated role in CE pathogenesis remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative bioinformatics and in vitro experiments to identify a diagnostic and therapeutic model for cirrhosis encephalopathy (CE) based on circadian rhythm and astrocyte-related genes. The authors validate the model's predictive ability and demonstrate its potential for guiding treatment, highlighting the combined role of circadian disruption and astrocyte dysfunction in CE.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS). The findings reveal common molecular signatures that may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and provide insights into the shared pathophysiology of these conditions.

papers.title: T cell antigenic recognition sequencing (TAR-seq) enables precise characterization of vaccine-elicited cellular immunity ex vivo and in vivo.
papers.abstract: The functional responses of antigen (Ag) specific T cells are complex, clonotype-specific, context-dependent, and incompletely captured by dominant analytic approaches. Here we present T Cell Antigenic Recognition Sequencing (TAR-seq), a two-part process that uses single-cell RNA + T cell receptor sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) to provide a precise and comprehensive characterization of the differentiation state and functional response of T cells specific to a given antigen, ex vivo and in vivo.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TAR-seq, a new method that combines single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing to comprehensively characterize antigen-specific T cell responses, including their differentiation state and functional profile, both ex vivo and in vivo. It offers a more precise and detailed approach compared to existing methods for studying vaccine-elicited cellular immunity.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals injury-responsive compartments and coordinated immune-fibrotic signaling in ANCA-associated renal vasculitis.
papers.abstract: ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) presents with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, yet the tissue-level molecular landscape in pediatric AAV remains poorly understood. We aimed to characterize spatially resolved renal disease programs across different histopathological stages of pediatric AAV and compared with adult AAV.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map the molecular landscape of kidney tissue in pediatric ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), revealing injury-responsive compartments and coordinated immune-fibrotic signaling across different histopathological stages. It provides a tissue-level view of the disease that was previously lacking, and compares pediatric with adult AAV to highlight shared and distinct molecular programs.

papers.title: Dual-graph attention autoencoder for spatial domain identification in ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables molecular mapping of ischemic stroke tissue, but spatial domain identification is challenging when injury disrupts normal tissue geometry. Methods relying on a single spatial-proximity graph cannot connect physically distant spots that share damage-associated transcriptional programs.
papers.summary: This paper presents a dual-graph attention autoencoder that improves spatial domain identification in ischemic stroke by integrating both spatial proximity and transcriptional similarity graphs, capturing damage-associated programs across distant spots. The method addresses limitations of single-graph approaches in disrupted tissue geometry.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms and Biomarkers Driving the Transition From Chronic Atrophic Gastritis to Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer continues to be a major contributor to global cancer morbidity and mortality. Although the Correa cascade is widely used as a model for gastric carcinogenesis, the molecular mechanisms driving the transition from chronic atrophic gastritis to invasive cancer have not been comprehensively integrated into a unified molecular framework. This review aims to synthesize current knowledge of the molecular events associated with each stage of the Correa cascade and to evaluate the clinical relevance of established and emerging biomarkers for risk stratification, early diagnosis, and per
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge of the molecular mechanisms driving the progression from chronic atrophic gastritis to gastric cancer, framed within the Correa cascade. It evaluates established and emerging biomarkers for their clinical utility in risk stratification, early diagnosis, and potentially personalized treatment, aiming to integrate these findings into a unified molecular framework.

papers.title: Spatial immune programs associated with nodal status differ between lymphoid follicular regions and peritumoral tonsillar tissue in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer.
papers.abstract: In human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), lymph node metastasis is common, yet its biological and prognostic implications remain incompletely understood. Less is known about the spatial organization of immune programs within tumor-associated secondary lymphoid structures.
papers.summary: This study maps the spatial organization of immune programs in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, comparing lymphoid follicular regions and peritumoral tonsillar tissue in relation to nodal status. It reveals that immune cell composition and activation states differ between these anatomical compartments and are associated with lymph node metastasis, providing new insights into the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: TGFBI in tumors and the tumor immune microenvironment: functional roles, mechanisms, and therapeutic targeting.
papers.abstract: TGFBI in tumors, providing a comprehensive theoretical foundation for developing TGFBI-based precision diagnosis and treatment. Transforming growth factor-beta-induced protein (TGFBI) is a secreted extracellular matrix protein involved in various physiological and pathological processes. Its multiple roles in tumorigenesis and the remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) have recently drawn increasing attention. This review systematically compares the dual pro-tumor and tumor-suppressive functions of TGFBI across multiple cancer types and provides a comprehensive analysis of its
papers.summary: This review systematically examines the dual roles of TGFBI in cancer, highlighting its context-dependent pro-tumor and tumor-suppressive functions across different cancer types and its impact on the tumor immune microenvironment. The authors provide a comprehensive analysis of the underlying mechanisms and discuss the potential of TGFBI as a therapeutic target for precision oncology.

papers.title: Targeted therapy against recurrent anti-synthetase syndrome associated interstitial lung disease after bilateral lung transplantation guided by transcriptomic analyses: a case-based study.
papers.abstract: Anti-synthetase syndrome (ASS) associated interstitial lung disease (ILD) usually responds to immunosuppressive therapy, but recurrence is common. We report a 58-year-old man with ASS-ILD who developed recurrent ILD within one year after bilateral lung transplantation (LTx). Despite triple immunosuppression (glucocorticoids, tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil), systemic inflammation persisted. This case represents an in vivo model of ASS-ILD recurrence, warranting further investigation into underlying mechanisms and novel therapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This case study reports a patient with anti-synthetase syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease who experienced disease recurrence after bilateral lung transplantation despite triple immunosuppression. Transcriptomic analyses guided targeted therapy, offering insights into the mechanisms of recurrence and potential novel treatment strategies.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify TRIP6 as a prognostic and EMT-associated biomarker in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound molecular heterogeneity and complex tumor-microenvironment interactions, which contribute to invasion, metastasis, and variable clinical outcomes. More effective prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets are still needed.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify TRIP6 as a novel prognostic biomarker associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in colorectal cancer. The findings suggest TRIP6 could serve as a potential therapeutic target, offering a new avenue for improving patient stratification and treatment.

papers.title: Targeting regulatory T cell plasticity in gastric cancer: a unified bimodal model and precision immunotherapy paradigm: a hypothesis-generating review.
papers.abstract: In contrast to other solid tumors, gastric cancer exhibits a particularly high dependence on regulatory T cell (Treg)-mediated immunosuppression. This reliance represents a critical driver of both primary and acquired resistance to programmed death-1/ligand-1(PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors. By integrating existing single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and clinical evidence, this review proposes a unified bimodal model of the Treg tumor microenvironment. Within this framework, the immune status in gastric cancer is determined by the dynamic equilibrium between immunosuppressive stable-type Tregs and pro
papers.summary: This hypothesis-generating review proposes a unified bimodal model of regulatory T cell (Treg) plasticity in gastric cancer, integrating single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and clinical evidence to explain resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. The model suggests that the balance between immunosuppressive stable-type Tregs and pro-inflammatory Treg subsets determines immune status, offering a framework for precision immunotherapy targeting Treg plasticity.

papers.title: CENPM as a biomarker and therapeutic target for lymph node metastasis in thyroid carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is a key prognostic determinant in thyroid carcinoma (THCA), yet molecular markers capturing intrinsic metastatic potential are limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies CENPM as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for lymph node metastasis in thyroid carcinoma, based on its differential expression and association with metastatic potential. The findings suggest that CENPM could help stratify patients at risk for LNM and serve as a target for future therapies.
